three_way_linguistic_experiment.title: 3-Way Linguistic Shift Experiment: English vs Tanglish vs Perturbed Tanglish
three_way_linguistic_experiment.description: Comparative analysis tracking prediction consistency and confidence decay as text transitions from formal English news structure to colloquial Tanglish, and finally into phonetically perturbed Tanglish.

groups.name: Standard English News Phrasing
groups.notes: Minimal out-of-vocabulary subwords; canonical word order.

groups.name: Natural Tanglish (Code-Mixed)
groups.notes: Dual language syntax; subword fragmentation increases.

groups.name: Perturbed Tanglish (Spelling & Transliteration Shifts)
groups.notes: Reveals vulnerability in mBERT subword segmenter; MuRIL remains robust.

three_way_linguistic_experiment.research_finding: Empirical Finding: While IndicBERT / mBERT exhibits near-perfect accuracy on canonical training samples, its prediction stability drops by 18.6% under real-world Tanglish phonetic and transliteration perturbations. Conversely, Google MuRIL exhibits superior resilience (91.8% stability, only 4.2% average confidence shift), validating the hypothesis that specialized Romanized Indic pre-training provides greater inductive bias for code-mixed social media intelligence.
